messages:
Maria: heads-up — us-west-2 GPU autoscaler started spiking provisioning attempts ~20m ago. Several new nodes ended up with the root filesystem remounted read-only due to nvme reassignments, then went NotReady. Seeing big provisioning churn and cost spike. :warning:
Rahul: ugh. any dmesg / kernel logs from affected hosts? which instance types?
Maria: i-0a3... (2 hosts so far: p4d-like pools). paste from one host:
```
[  123.456789] nvme0: detected SMART error, reassigning LBA
[  123.456800] nvme0n1: reassign_range error, device_in_recovery=1
[  123.456901] EXT4-fs error (device nvme0n1): ext4_journal_check_start: Detected aborted journal
[  123.456902] EXT4-fs (nvme0n1): Remounted filesystem read-only
```

Rahul: that looks like device-level reassigns (pending sector remap). Did SMART report failing sectors? run `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1` if available.
Maria: ran quick SMART, here's the critical bits:
```
SMART overall-health self-assessment test result: FAILED
Data Units Written: 1023 TB
Media and Data Integrity Errors: 12
Warning_Level: critical
```

Nicole: 12 integrity errors + >1PB written — fleet age + write-heavy workloads (scratch / cache) piling up. Not the first time for this AZ.
Joel: how did autoscaler react? did it kick out faulty nodes or try to reuse them?
Maria: autoscaler kept treating them as provisioned because instance came up and kubelet registered, but then node transitions to NotReady quickly. Our capacity controller then launched replacements in same AZ until quota exhausted. Net effect: 8 extra nodes launched in us-west-2 over 15m, billing / provisioning backlog.
ops-bot: ALERT: nvme-readonly-remounts detected — 6 hosts in us-west-2, severity=high, incident=INC-2026-432.
Rahul: root cause chain seems to be: (1) older ephemeral NVMe devices hitting wear -> SMART reassigns -> read-only remount, (2) node health signal reported as Ready briefly so autoscaler counts capacity, (3) autoscaler keeps launching in same AZ due to zone preference -> capacity thrash and cost.
Nicole: immediate mitigation suggestions:
- flip autoscaler zone bias away from us-west-2 (manual policy)
- pause autoscaler or reduce max surge for GPU pools
- add a quick node-probe to treat early read-only remounts as unhealthy (kubelet/hc change)

Rahul: i can push a hotfix to the scaler config: prefer us-east-1 & us-west-1, reduce max_unready 0.1 -> 0.02. applying in 2m.
Maria: please also add a taint to existing suspicious nodes `node.kubernetes.io/ephemeral-nvme-failing:NoSchedule` so new pods won't land.
Joel: longer-term: we should stop counting transient Ready states as "usable" until node passes a short IO healthcheck. Proposal: on join, run `dd if=/dev/nvme0n1 of=/dev/null bs=1M count=16` and check for IO errors before offering for pod scheduling. Low overhead but catches remap errors.
Nicole: also consider reducing ephemeral-cleaner IO pressure — it does aggressive scrub/truncation on scratch directories during deprovision and that likely increases write amplification on worn drives. Lower concurrency for GC for older instances.
Rahul: pushed autoscaler policy change, reduced AZ bias, and lowered surge. Watching.
Maria: operations log of actions taken:
- 19:02 UTC: applied autoscaler policy change (moved away from us-west-2)
- 19:04 UTC: tainted 6 suspect nodes
- 19:06 UTC: suspended ephemeral-cleaner cron for us-west-2 pool
- 19:10 UTC: scaled down replacement launchers (prevent further churn)

ops-bot: Incident note updated: mitigations applied, monitoring for 2h.
Nicole: follow-ups for postmortem:
- fix autoscaler health gating to use IO sanity check on node join (owner: eng-infra)
- add nvme wear metrics to fleet dashboard, trigger proactive retirement at >800 TB written or >5 media errors (owner: eng-ml + infra)
- reduce ephemeral-cleaner concurrency by default in older hardware pools (owner: eng-runtime)
- quota/backoff policy tweak: if >3 sequential node failures in AZ, backoff and shift zones (owner: infra-ops)

Rahul: agreed. i will open PRs for the autoscaler gating and the surge/zone backoff rule.
Maria: cost impact estimate — ~8 extra p4d-hour equivalents billed, roughly $42k on the bill if sustained for an hour. We stopped within 20m so actual is ~14k spike. Add to incident cost note.
Joel: will run a canary test of the IO probe on a small fleet next week.
Maria: thanks all. keep me posted if any hosts flip to read-only again. :thumbsup:
